title: Data Sharing Agreement - Oakland Enrolls - Student Enrollment Office
official_text:
Approval of Data Sharing Agreement by and between Oakland Enrolls and District, for the purpose of evaluating information relating to enrollment patterns pursuant to OUSD Board Policy 6006, entitled Quality School Development: Community of Schools (“BP 6006”), supporting the study of enrollment patterns to provide quality, equitable education to all Oakland students; and prepare one or more Reports of the findings as stated in Agreement, for the term February 27, 2020 through July 1, 2023, at no cost to the District. *
__
*This Data Sharing Agreement is responsive to previous concerns raised about a two-way data sharing agreement. Under this agreement, Oakland Enrolls (the charter application platform) will share student-level data with the District for the District’s analytic purposes. Any aggregate reports produced using this data will be shared back with Oakland Enrolls, but those reports will not include any student-level or identifiable information for District students.
headline: Approves a no-cost data sharing agreement with Oakland Enrolls to study enrollment patterns through 2023
summary: Oakland Enrolls, the charter application platform, will share student-level data with the district so the district can study enrollment patterns and write reports. Aggregate reports will be shared back with Oakland Enrolls but will not include student-level or identifiable information. The agreement runs from February 27, 2020 through July 1, 2023 and costs the district nothing.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Contract - Luis A Lopez Lara - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text:
Ratification by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Contract between the District and Luis A Lopez Lara, Oakland, CA, for the latter to virtually provide an additional 114 hours of
Alcohol, Tobacco & Other Drugs (ATOD) awareness sessions for students violating OUSD tobacco/drug free policies, cessation and strengths-based life skills and behavior coaching at Madison Park Academy 6-12 school site in coordination with the site's COST and administrative team and school site staff, for the period of October 09, 2019 through May 29, 2020, in the additional amount of $4,000.00, increasing the Contract not to exceed amount from $4,480.00 to $8,480.00 and COVID Amendment, via the Community Schools and Student Services Department.  All other terms and conditions of the Contract remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $4,000 to a contract for drug and tobacco awareness sessions at Madison Park Academy
summary: The district is ratifying an amendment to a professional services contract with an individual contractor for 114 more hours of virtual alcohol, tobacco and other drugs awareness sessions, life skills and behavior coaching for students at Madison Park Academy 6-12 who violated the district's tobacco and drug-free policies. It adds $4,000.00 and raises the contract limit from $4,480.00 to $8,480.00 for October 9, 2019 through May 29, 2020. Ratification means the board is approving it after it has already begun.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: COVID Amendment – NonPublic, Nonsectarian School/Agency Services Master Contract – Resolution No. 1920-0151 – Named Contractor - Special Education Department
official_text:
Adoption by the Board of Education of COVID Amendment by and between District and
§	La Cheim School, Inc., El Sobrante, CA; and
§	Star Academy, San Rafael, CA
amending Non-Public School/Agency Master Contract Resolution No. 1920-0151, (Legislative File Id No. 19-1716, Enactment No 19-1376, adopted September 11, 2019), in part, pertaining only to the Contract with named vendor, necessary in light of the COVID-19 Pandemic and the shelter-in-place order issued by the Alameda County Public Health Officer, and/or other authorities within and without California, modifying, among other provisions, the Scope of Work, enabling the vendor to provide the services described in the original Contract - Scope of Work - by any means that are consistent with COVID-19-related local, state, and federal orders (including providing the services virtually), as long as the District agrees in writing and adding a requirement for more information to be provided in an Invoice, and authoring no additional costs for said services. All other terms and conditions of the Contract remain in full force and effect.
headline: Lets two nonpublic special-education schools serve students virtually at no added cost
summary: This amends the district’s master contract with nonpublic schools and agencies for two named vendors, La Cheim School and Star Academy. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, they may deliver services by any means allowed under health orders, including virtually, if the district agrees in writing, and invoices must include more information. There is no additional cost, and all other contract terms stay the same.
vendor_name: La Cheim School, Inc.; Star Academy
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Performance Fact - Network 4
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and Performance Fact, Oakland, CA, after four years of design, development, implementation, and continuous improvement of a number of promising practices at the Lockwood Elementary School Campus, through the School Improvement Grant, at the Network level, and at the LEA (Oakland USD) level, for the latter to provide three strands: 

Strand #1: Assess SIG’s Impact
Assess and document “what we did, what difference it made, what we
learned” during the years of SIG implementation at the Lockwood Campus,
Network, and LEA levels, including compilation and analysis of evidence such as:
artifacts, video/photos, interviews and surveys, student outcome data, impact
on/of teaching, learning, leadership, and operations;
.
Strand #2: Design for Post-SIG Sustainability
Codify core tools and processes, including full documentation in digital formats
(e.g., Google Suite) that ensure easy access and wide dissemination, and
facilitators who would possess the knowledge and skills to serve as trainers for
others regarding the core tools and processes; and 

Strand #3: Focus Implementation in COVID-19 Era
Provide technical assistance regarding implementation of the specific 2020-
2021 annual priorities (i.e., work plan) at the Lockwood Campus, the Network,
and the LEA, with adjustments for the COVID-19 environment,

via Network 4,  for the period of December 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $195,000.00.

title: Amendment No. 1, Memorandum of Understanding - Bay Area Community Resources - Learning Pod - Sankofa United Elementary School
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Memorandum of Understanding between the District and Bay Area Community Resources, San Rafael, CA, adding to the Scope of Work set forth in the August 26, 2020 Agreement (Legislative File No. 20-1178, Enactment No. 20-1206) the following paragraphs to the existing Scope of Work: 

Amended Scope of Work

VENDOR will provide in-person learning supports to students in K-5 at Sankofa United Elementary School. In-person learning supports may include (but are not limited to) support with accessing technology, facilitating access to classroom zoom sessions, motivating students to complete work, providing one-to-one mentoring or encouragement, and connecting with supplemental services if needed, and other supports as directed by OUSD.

As set forth in Paragraph 4 of this Amendment, VENDOR agrees to perform these services in accordance with any shelter-in-place (or similar) orders (“SIP orders”), and to immediately follow all OUSD directives regarding health and safety protocols. Specifically, VENDOR shall deliver services in cohorts with student: staff ratios that comply with SIP orders and OUSD directives. In addition, VENDOR shall ensure that all staff participate in wellness checks (including proof of negative COVID-19 test results) in accordance with OUSD policies and directives 

All other terms and condition of the Memorandum of Understanding remain in full force and effect.
funding_source: After School Education and Safety (ASES) Grant, 21st Century Community Learning Centers Grant
headline: Expands Bay Area Community Resources' scope to add in-person learning support at Sankofa United Elementary
summary: This changes an existing agreement with Bay Area Community Resources, a San Rafael organization, to add in-person learning support for K-5 students at Sankofa United Elementary School. Support can include help with technology and online classes, mentoring and connecting students to other services, following shelter-in-place orders and health rules. The text states no dollar amount, and all other terms stay the same.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of Stevenson-Wyler Short-Form Cooperative Research & Development Agreement between the Regents of the University of California, on behalf of its Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (EOLBNL), and the District, as the latter prepares to reopen its K-12 classroom, and is considering the adequacy of its current heating, ventilation and air-condition systems (HVAC) in classrooms, for EOLBNL to provide technical assistance to the District in its review of guidance and best practices for reducing aerosol transmission risk and to work with District in selecting indoor air quality (IAQ) monitors as part of longer term strategies to ensure adequate ventilation in K-12 classroom, via the Facilities Planning and Management Division, for the term of January 29, 2021, through March 31, 2021, with the District providing $0 cash and a $1,350.00 in-kind contribution and the Regents though its contract with U.S. Department of Energy (USDOE) contributing $10,000.00, subject to available funding.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Ratifies a no-cost research partnership with Berkeley Lab on classroom air quality and ventilation
summary: The district is partnering with the University of California's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, which will give technical help on reducing the spread of airborne germs and on choosing indoor air quality monitors as schools reopen. The district puts in no cash and $1,350 of in-kind contribution, while the University contributes $10,000 through its U.S. Department of Energy contract. The agreement ran from January 29 to March 31, 2021, which began before the board vote.
vendor_name: Regents of the University of California (Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Agreement - R&D Consultants - Burckhalter Elementary School

group: Measure N Commission - February 2, 2021 Jason Gumataotao, Chairperson
title: Measure N Commission - 2020-2021 Budget Modification - Castlemont High School
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of Measure N Commission, of a 2020-2021 budget modification request from Castlemont High School transferring the total amount of $7,795.00 from two different strategic actions; Supplies & Materials (no impact, given the time left in the year and nothing has been spent so far on this action) to Consultant Contracts to hire Oakland Kids First to provide stipends for school year and summer internships, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
presenter: Measure N - College and Career Readiness Commission
headline: Moves $7,795 at Castlemont High to pay Oakland Kids First for student internship stipends
summary: The Measure N Commission recommends shifting $7,795.00 within Castlemont High School's 2020-21 Measure N budget. The money comes from the supplies and materials line, where nothing has been spent so far, and goes to a consultant contract with Oakland Kids First for stipends for school-year and summer internships.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Measure N Commission - February 2, 2021 Jason Gumataotao, Chairperson
title: Measure N Commission - 2020-2021 Budget Modification - Skyline High School
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of Measure N Commission, of a 2020-2021 budget modification request from Skyline High School transferring $13,125.00 from four different strategic actions; $5,000 from Transportation Costs, $3,125 from Teacher Substitutes, $4,000 from Transportation Costs, and $1,000 from AC Transit/BART Tickets (little to no impact- travel, field trips, conferences and substitutes not needed) to Teacher Salaries Stipends for Extended Contracts for Collaboration / PD Time, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.
presenter: Measure N - College and Career Readiness Commission
headline: Moves $13,125 at Skyline High from travel and substitute funds to teacher collaboration stipends
summary: The Measure N Commission recommends shifting $13,125.00 within Skyline High School's 2020-21 Measure N budget. The money comes from four lines (transportation costs, teacher substitutes and AC Transit/BART tickets) and goes to stipends for teachers on extended contracts for collaboration and professional development time. The request says travel, field trips, conferences and substitutes are not needed, so there is little to no impact.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Planting Justice - Dewey Academy
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and Planting Justice, Oakland, CA, for the latter to offer nutrition education that will enable students to test real-life nutritional situations; educate the students on nutrition, and the study of nutrients in food, how the body uses nutrients, and the relationship between diet, health, and disease and provide related information at Dewey Academy, for the period of April 12, 2021 through June 30, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $13,400.00.

The period is April 12 through June 30, 2021, capped at $13,400. The Board is approving this after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Soccer Without Borders - Oakland International High School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 between the District and Soccer Without Borders, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide (1) a program director, education coordinator, and boy's and girls’ soccer coach to (2) support home visits to OIHS students and families; (3) coordinate a minimum of 16 Wellness workshops; (4) conduct outreach and screening of all students before entering the program; (5) plan and coordinate Manhood Development workshops with the OIHS Dean of Students, serving a total of  25 high-risk students in bi-weekly small group sessions; (6) offer educational workshops and support wellness events in the school community; (7) support with conflict mediation between and among students, and between staff and students; (8) contribute to school’s culture of youth leadership and restorative justice-based community building at Oakland International High School, for the period of September 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, in an amount not to exceed $13,000.00.
headline: Pays Soccer Without Borders up to $13,000 for wellness and soccer programs at Oakland International High
summary: Soccer Without Borders will provide a program director, education coordinator and soccer coaches at Oakland International High School. They will support home visits, run wellness and Manhood Development workshops for 25 high-risk students, and help with conflict mediation. The period is September 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, capped at $13,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Rachelle Rogers-Ard - Claremont Middle School

official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 1, Agreement by and between the District and Redgwick Construction Company, Oakland, CA, for a time extension only for the Horace Mann Elementary School Retaining Wall & Stair Replacement Project, due to weather delays, extending the term of the Agreement from December 10, 2020 through March 10, 2021 to July 31, 2021 (an additional 143 days). All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Extends Horace Mann retaining wall and stair project to July 31, 2021 after weather delays; no added cost
summary: This change order gives Redgwick Construction Company more time, and only more time, to finish the Horace Mann Elementary School Retaining Wall & Stair Replacement Project because of weather delays. The end date moves from March 10, 2021 to July 31, 2021, an additional 143 days. The original end date had already passed when the Board was asked to approve this, and all other terms stay in effect.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

group: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
title: Joint Use Lease Agreement - Former Webster Child Development Center - Unity Council - Oakland Unified School District
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of the Joint Use Lease Agreement by and between the District and Unity Council, Oakland, CA, for occupancy of a portion of the Former Webster Child Development Center (“CDC”) Property, for $60,000 annually, with an annual Rent adjustment of no more than a 3% per Annum, for the term July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2026.
headline: Leases part of the former Webster Child Development Center to Unity Council for $60,000 a year
summary: The Board approves a joint use lease letting Unity Council occupy a portion of the former Webster Child Development Center property for $60,000 a year. Rent may rise by no more than 3% per year. The lease runs July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2026.
pulled_from_consent: Adopted in its own vote at this meeting (7–0), instead of with the rest of the consent report.
outcome_action: Adopted

title: Creation/Revision of Job Descriptions – Named Positions – Talent/Human Resources Department
headline: Creates five job descriptions and revises three, including a Grants Manager and a Chief Governance Officer

outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

official_text: Approval by the Board of Education, upon recommendation of the Facilities Committee, of Construction Management Agreement by and between the District and Sixth Dimension, LLC, Oakland, CA for the latter to provide planning, coordination and program management services through the completion of the District’s Measure J and commencement of Measure Y Bond Programs for Construction Management Services for Facilities Planning & Management Project, as follows: in the not to exceed amount of $900,000.00: not to exceed the amount of $780,000.00 for Basic Services on all Assignments (Section 2A); not to exceed the amount of $45,000.00 for Reimbursable Expenses for all Assignments (Section 2B); and not to exceed the amount of $75,000.00 for Additional Services on all Assignments (Section 2F); each as specified, with work scheduled to commence on August 26, 2021, and scheduled to last until June 30, 2026, pursuant to the Agreement.
headline: Hires Sixth Dimension to manage facilities bond planning for up to $900,000 through 2026
summary: The district is hiring Sixth Dimension, LLC of Oakland to provide planning, coordination and program management for school construction work funded by the Measure J and Measure Y bonds. The total is capped at $900,000: $780,000 for basic services, $45,000 for reimbursable expenses and $75,000 for additional services. Work is scheduled to start August 26, 2021 and run until June 30, 2026.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding - Regents of the University of California, Et Al - Participation In The Berkeley Psychology Internship Consortium
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding by and between the Regents of the University of California on behalf of the Graduate School of Education at the Berkeley Campus, the San Francisco Unified School District, the Piedmont Unified School District and the Oakland Unified School District (District), in which the Parities mutually agree, pursuant to terms and conditions of the MOU, that it is in their interest to participate in a training program for doctoral level psychology student interns, to be known as the Berkeley Psychology Internship Consortium (BPIC) , which will provide placement and practicum for 2-4 interns in District per year with District pupils, particularly Special Education Program pupils, receiving psychological services, for  a term of two years, unless terminated earlier as set forth in MOU, commencing upon execution by the Parties and approval by the participating school district’s governing board, at an annual stipend of $25,000.00 per intern, for a total amount not to exceed $200,000.00 per year.
headline: Pays up to $200,000 a year to join a UC Berkeley psychology intern program serving OUSD students

The district pays a $25,000 stipend per intern, up to $200,000 per year.

title: First 5 (Five) of Alameda County - Contract for Services - Kindergarten Readiness - Neighborhoods Ready for School - Summer Learning Programs - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Contract for Services (Contract Number PI-NRS-2122-658) by and between the District and First 5 of Alameda County, Alameda, CA, with District accepting Grant Award from the latter, in the amount of $531,958.00, to support Summer Pre-K (SPK) programs and provide Early Childhood Education (ECE) and K-12 teachers with professional development and orientation to the SPK model; support a School Readiness Coordinator (Program Manager) to develop and implement year-round school readiness and transition programming including a student passport/snapshot form, a variety of family/child learning activities, and to provide financial relief to families with children 0-5 through the Oakland Educational Fund for the highest need families residing in the highest need  neighborhoods in the City of Oakland, serving all Child Development Centers (CDC) and  participating Summer Pre-K sites, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Contract.
funding_source: First Five of Alameda County Grant
headline: Accepts $531,958 from First 5 of Alameda County for Summer Pre-K and school readiness work
summary: The district accepts a grant from First 5 of Alameda County to support Summer Pre-K programs and give early childhood and K-12 teachers training on the Summer Pre-K model. It also pays for a School Readiness Coordinator and financial relief for families with children ages 0-5 in the highest-need Oakland neighborhoods. The contract runs July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Sole Source Exception To Public Bidding - Services Agreement - COVID-19 Testing – Spartan Medical, Inc. – Office of the Chief of Staff
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution 2122-0108 - Authorizing Use of Sole Source Exception to Public Bidding for a Services Agreement by and between the District and Spartan Medical, Inc., a Maryland Corporation, for the latter to provide site coordinators or medical staff (“Professionals”) at each customer site designated by OUSD to assist with District’s COVID-19 testing program to be conducted, for the period of October 13, 2021 through October 12, 2022, in an amount not-to-exceed $3,672,000.00.
headline: Pays Spartan Medical up to $3.67M for COVID-19 testing site staff, without public bidding
summary: The district hires Spartan Medical, Inc., a Maryland company, to provide site coordinators or medical staff for its COVID-19 testing program from October 13, 2021 through October 12, 2022. The Board is using a legal exception that lets the district skip public bidding because the vendor is the sole source.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Teaching Strategies, LLC, Bethesda, MD, for the latter to provide Professional Development for teachers and staff on, Getting started with teaching strategies for preschool, Responsive planning and meeting the needs of Children and families and Meaningful experiences using in - Depth Investigations to support Learning, via the Early Childhood Development Department, for the period of October 11, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $79,920.00.

official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide one (1) resident artist to work in a side by side model during in person instruction, with the goal to provide arts integration for each of K-2 classes in cycles of 6  weeks each, for 1 hour during Math or ELA class time; lessons design in collaboration with the classroom teacher to correlate with subject pacing and state standards at Hoover Elementary School, for the period of August 23, 2021 through May 26, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $22,500.00.

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - William L. Winston, Education Consulting LLC - Talent / Human Resources Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and William L. Winston, Education Consulting LLC, Oakland, CA, for the latter to ensure that partnership with colleges and universities for new teacher recruitment and pipelines are developed and maintained through development of Memorandums of Understanding, including Initiating contact with the designated staff at the college responsible for the MOU, communicating with the college and university partners about the MOU process, the writing of the MOU, and the negotiation of the MOU content, receiving approval from the District’s Legal Department, submitting and tracking the MOU through the approval process, via Talent / Human Resources Department, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00.

title: Memorandum of Understanding - OUSD STEM Teacher Pathway and Mentor Fellow Project 2021-22 - Trellis Education - Talent/Human Resources Department

outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Design For Equity LLC - Madison Park Academy (Upper Campus)
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Design For Equity, LLC, Oakland, CA, for the latter, over a ten (10) month period, in consultation with the school site team, to provide transformative professional learning experiences to the facility and staff to build individual and group capacity to interrupt and change inequitable teaching practices, policies and structures and shift the culture of the school toward creating greater racial equity and belonging, as described in Exhibit A, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, at Madison Park Academy (Upper Campus), for the period of August 11, 2021 through May 11, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00.
headline: Ratifies $25,000 for Design For Equity's teacher learning on racial equity at Madison Park Academy
summary: Design For Equity LLC will lead professional learning for staff at Madison Park Academy (Upper Campus) over ten months. The sessions aim to change teaching practices, policies and structures that are unfair and build a school culture of racial equity and belonging. The cost is up to $25,000 for August 11, 2021 through May 11, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Fifth Amendment, Office Lease - Sparknight, LLC - Central Administrative Offices - 1000 Broadway, Oakland, CA
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Fifth Amendment, Lease Agreement by and between the Oakland Unified School District (“District) as lessee, and Sparknight, LLC, a Florida limited liability company, as lessor (“Lessor”), for space within the building located at 1000 Broadway, Oakland, CA 94607, commonly known as the Transpacific Centre, in which the  District and Lessor propose to: (1) further extend the termination date of the Original Lease, as amended, by one year to August 31, 2023; (2) reduce the premises rented by the District from Lessor by calling for the District to surrender Suite 300 back to the Lessor; (3) establish the amount of monthly base rent to be owed by the District to the Lessor; (4) describe the District’s and Lessor’s rights and obligations with regard to certain move‐out and close‐out procedures to be performed by District with regard to Suite 300; (5) grant the District the option to extend the termination date of the Lease by one additional period of six months; and (6) modify the rights of the District to parking at the Property, for $2,501,550.00 total annual rent under the Fifth Amendment, for the term of September 1, 2022 through August 31, 2023.
headline: Extends the district's Broadway office lease one year at $2.5M a year and gives up Suite 300
summary: This fifth amendment to the lease for the central administrative offices at 1000 Broadway extends the lease by one year to August 31, 2023. The district will give Suite 300 back to the landlord, Sparknight, LLC, and a new monthly base rent is set. The district also gets an option to extend six more months, and its parking rights change. Total annual rent is $2,501,550.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: First Addendum, Charter School Facilities Program Use Agreement - Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy - Office of Charter Schools
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of the First Addendum to Charter School Facilities Program Use Agreement For Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy, by and between the District and Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy, pursuant to terms and conditions stated therein including:

Starting in the 2021-22 fiscal year and continuing through the 2054-55 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay the following facilities use fee on a yearly basis: 

	(a) Starting in the 2021-2022 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 0.5% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(b) Starting in the 2030-31 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 0.75% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(c) Starting in the 2040-41 fiscal year, the Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 1% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(d) Starting in the 2050-51 fiscal year, the Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 2% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

However, for any school year in which the percentage of out-of-district students enrolled at Charter School is greater than ten percent (10%) on “Census Day” of that school year, the yearly facilities use fee shall be calculated as follows: 1) Fees shall be calculated pursuant to (a) through (d), above, for the percentage of enrollment that comprise in-District students, and 2) Fees shall be calculated pursuant to (e) through (h), below, for the percentage of enrollment that comprise out of District students. 

	(e) Starting in the 2021-2022 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 0.95% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined in Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(f) Starting in the 2030-2031 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 1.2% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined by Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 

	(g) Starting in the 2040-2041 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 1.45% of the yearly revenue of the Charter school, as defined by Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f).

	(h) Starting in the 2050-2051 fiscal year, Charter School shall pay a fee in the amount of 2.45% of the yearly revenue of the Charter School, as defined by Education Code section 47613, subdivision (f). 
	
All other terms of the Use Agreement remain unchanged and in full force and effect and apply to the terms set forth in the First Addendum.
headline: Sets facilities fees Lazear Charter Academy pays the district, 0.5% to 2% of revenue through 2055
summary: This first addendum sets a yearly facilities use fee that Education for Change Public Schools - Lazear Charter Academy pays the district. The fee is a percentage of the charter school's yearly revenue and rises in steps, from 0.5% in 2021-22 to 2% starting in 2050-51, through 2054-55. Higher percentages apply to the share of students who live outside the district when out-of-district enrollment is above 10%.

title: Electricity Service Agreement – East Bay Community Energy Authority – Oakland Unified School District Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0212 - Declaring the Futility of Public Bidding for Electricity Service and Approving a Contract for that Purchase, the Electricity Service Agreement by and between the District and East Bay Community Energy Authority, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide favorable, fixed electricity rates discounted from EBCE’s standard electricity rates for the District’s direct access-eligible electric energy services agreements as consideration for the District’s long-term commitment as an electricity customer of EBCE, with an Initial Term to begin on May 1, 2022, and end on April 30, 2024, for a two (2) year total amount not to exceed $1,500,000 to $2,500,000 for the Initial Term, a non-binding estimate based on the District’s historic electricity usage trend; if the District’s electricity usage increases significantly during the Initial Term, the range would similarly increase.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Signs two-year electricity deal with East Bay Community Energy, estimated $1.5M to $2.5M
summary: The district would buy electricity from East Bay Community Energy Authority at fixed rates below the authority's standard rates, in return for a long-term commitment as a customer. The first term runs May 1, 2022 through April 30, 2024, with a non-binding estimate of $1,500,000 to $2,500,000 that would rise if usage rises significantly. The board is declaring that public bidding would be futile, so the district is not running its own bid.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

The agreement is managed by the Linked Learning Department and runs from July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
vendor_name: The Regents of the University of California, San Francisco Campus
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - The Crucible - OPSR Counseling Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and The Crucible, Oakland, CA, for the latter to inspire creative exploration and expression through welcoming, hands-on arts education and experiences for District’s 9th & 10th graders in the Central Academic Recovery summer learning experience, providing on site arts projects in collaboration with the credentialed Geometry teacher built around the industrial arts and the content area foci; provide hands experience in leather/textiles to promote skills in design, measurement, layout, and fabrication; provide information about general construction of leather goods as well as the application of skills developed and how to apply them to a variety of projects and related activities, as stated in Exhibit A of the Agreement, via OPSR Counseling Department, for the period of June 2, 2022, through July 8, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $4,000.00.
headline: Pays The Crucible up to $4,000 for a summer leatherworking class for 9th and 10th graders
summary: The Crucible will provide hands-on arts projects in leather and textiles for 9th and 10th graders in the district's Central Academic Recovery summer learning experience, working with the Geometry teacher. The agreement runs from June 2 to July 8, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Sonia Spindt - Coliseum College Preparatory Academy
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Sonia Spindt, Golden, CO, for latter (former computer science lead teacher) to serve as the new Computer Science consultant to provide services by creating the Computer Science (CS) curriculum and professional development, i.e., to develop a rigorous curriculum for the CS pathway, specifically serving 11th and 12th graders, to better prepare students for college courses success and post-high school schooling and work force, as stated in Exhibit A of Agreement, at Coliseum College Preparatory Academy, for the period of July 1, 2021 through May 26, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $8,000.00.
headline: Pays a computer science consultant up to $8,000 to build a curriculum at Coliseum College Prep
summary: An individual consultant, a former computer science lead teacher, will create the computer science curriculum and professional development for the 11th and 12th grade pathway at Coliseum College Preparatory Academy. The agreement runs from July 1, 2021 to May 26, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - The Regents of the University of California - Center for Educational Partnerships - Oakland High School
official_text:
Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and The Regents of the University of California, Center for Educational Partnerships, Berkeley, CA, for its 
Destination College Advising Corps (DCAC) to train, mentor and assign a fulltime, dedicated College Adviser Fellow to provide mentorship, promote college and career going culture through guidance and supervision of a Regional Manager at Oakland High School, for the period of August 2, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $18,000.00.
headline: Pays UC's Destination College Advising Corps up to $18,000 for a college adviser at Oakland High
summary: The University of California's Center for Educational Partnerships, through its Destination College Advising Corps, will train, mentor and assign a full-time College Adviser Fellow at Oakland High School to promote a college- and career-going culture. The agreement runs from August 2, 2021 to June 30, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
vendor_name: The Regents of the University of California, Center for Educational Partnerships
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Groundwork Education - Linked Learning Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Groundwork Education, Berkeley, CA, for the latter to provide Emergency Medical Services workshops and opportunities for certification for 30 students newcomer students, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, at Rudsdale Newcomer School, via Linked Learning Department, for the period of April 11, 2022 through May 25, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $15,540.00.
headline: Pays Groundwork Education up to $15,540 for emergency medical training for newcomer students
summary: Groundwork Education will offer Emergency Medical Services workshops and a chance to earn certification for 30 newcomer students at Rudsdale Newcomer School, through the Linked Learning Department. The agreement runs from April 11 to May 25, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Oakland Youth Chorus - Claremont Middle School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Oakland Youth Chorus, Oakland, CA, for the latter to support the school in designing, creating, implementing and evaluating a school based music program whether through virtual, in person or a hybrid program delivery model, as set forth in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, at Claremont Middle School, for the period of August 28, 2021 through May 26, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00.
headline: Pays Oakland Youth Chorus up to $20,000 to build a music program at Claremont Middle School
summary: Oakland Youth Chorus will help Claremont Middle School design, create, carry out and evaluate a school-based music program, delivered virtually, in person or in a hybrid format. The agreement runs from August 28, 2021 to May 26, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc - OPSR Counseling Department
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc, Oakland, CA, for the latter, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement,  to partner with District’s Central Academic Recovery team’s summer learning experience for 9th & 10th graders to empower, inspire self-awareness through art, creativity and education, with participants  learning to make positive choices to break the cycle of violence for themselves and their
communities, choose peace over conflict and love over fear, via OPSR Counseling Department, for the period of June 2, 2022 through July 8, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00.
headline: Pays Attitudinal Healing Connection up to $5,000 for summer peace and creativity sessions
summary: Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc. will join the district's Central Academic Recovery summer learning experience for 9th and 10th graders, using art, creativity and education to build self-awareness and help students choose peace over conflict. The agreement runs from June 2 to July 8, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Mills College - LIFE Academy
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Mills College, Oakland, CA, for the latter to support the school’s Multi-Tiered Systems of Support team by creating and facilitating a customized workshop for the team in early June that will support school to use what has been learned about supporting students with academic, attendance and behavioral needs and to plan for next school year with goals and students at the center, stated in Exhibit A of Agreement,  for LIFE Academy, for the period of May 30, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $4,000.00.
headline: Pays Mills College up to $4,000 for a student-support planning workshop at LIFE Academy
summary: Mills College will create and lead a customized workshop in early June for the Multi-Tiered Systems of Support team at LIFE Academy. The team will use it to review how it supports students with academic, attendance and behavior needs and to plan for next school year. The agreement runs from May 30 to June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Rigorous Love - LIFE Academy
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Rigorous Love, Oakland, CA, for the latter to support parent group, Parent Academy, with two professional learning sessions to be held in both Spanish and English, with the first being on anti-Black racism within the Raza community and the second being on Restorative Justice and the circle process and school’s approach to discipline through a restorative lens, as stated in Exhibit A of Agreement, at  Life Academy, for the period of May 2, 2022 through May 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $2,060.00.
headline: Pays Rigorous Love up to $2,060 for two parent learning sessions at LIFE Academy
summary: Rigorous Love will lead two professional learning sessions for the school's Parent Academy, held in both Spanish and English. One covers anti-Black racism within the Raza community, and the other covers restorative justice and the school's approach to discipline. The agreement runs from May 2 to May 30, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Hillary Walker - LIFE Academy
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Hillary Walker, Oakland, CA, for the latter to plan and co-lead a group of students on a public health pathway "post session" through which 20 pathways students will be exposed to a variety of public health experiences linked to their pathway projects, including a week long out of state public health field trip connected to the post session and projects, as stated in Exhibit A of Agreement at Life Academy, for the period of April 1, 2022 through May 26, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $8,000.00.
headline: Pays a consultant up to $8,000 to lead a public health pathway trip for LIFE Academy students
summary: An individual contractor will plan and co-lead a public health pathway "post session" for 20 students at LIFE Academy. It includes a week-long out-of-state public health field trip tied to their pathway projects. The agreement runs from April 1 to May 26, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Earth Team - Skyline High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Earth Team, Richmond, CA, for the latter to provide opportunities for students to engage in real world work experiences through their Sustainable Youth Program, a long term approach to environmental education by working with individual core schools to offer a variety of projects-from short-term class visits to yearlong after school internships-all with a multi-year approach that caters to the unique needs of students and their respective schools with this year’s  projects focusing on waste, watersheds, litter and a brand new urban forestry project, stated in Exhibit A of Agreement,  at Skyline High School, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,600.00.
headline: Pays Earth Team up to $5,600 for environmental work experiences at Skyline High School
summary: Earth Team will offer students real-world work experience through its Sustainable Youth Program, with projects this year on waste, watersheds, litter and a new urban forestry project at Skyline High School. The agreement runs from July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Global Seed - Oakland High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Global Seed, Oakland, CA, for the latter to manage and coordinate Y-PLAN Oakland action research projects and partnerships between teachers and civic clients by fostering development of key partners and stakeholders within District, the city, and the region, and developing civic work-based learning projects for 2021-22, with this Agreement, as delineated in Exhibit A, to improve student engagement in  Pathways  by empowering students through community-based action research projects that create more relevant and dynamic learning opportunities for Oakland High School, for the period of August 9, 2021 through May 31, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00.
headline: Pays Global Seed up to $10,000 to run student research projects at Oakland High
summary: Global Seed will manage and coordinate Y-PLAN Oakland, which links teachers with civic partners on community-based action research projects. The goal is to make Pathways learning more relevant for students at Oakland High School. The agreement runs from August 9, 2021 to May 31, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Niroga Institute - OPSR Counseling Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Niroga Institute, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a trained instructor to collaborate alongside a credentialed Biology teacher to implement its vision of creating a mindful generation for a more connected and compassionate world as an extension of the NGSS aligned Biology unit about the Stress Response;  promote equity by teaching students and adults trauma-informed dynamic mindfulness, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, via OPSR Counseling Department, for the period of June 2, 2022, through July 8, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $4,500.00.
headline: Pays Niroga Institute up to $4,500 to teach mindfulness alongside a biology unit
summary: Niroga Institute will provide a trained instructor to work with a Biology teacher, extending a biology unit on the stress response by teaching students and adults trauma-informed mindfulness. It is arranged through the OPSR Counseling Department and runs from June 2 to July 8, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Skyline High School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide students with mental health support including regular one-on-one meetings and group sessions for students; coordinate with Coordination of Services Team (COST), Leadership Team, and Culture Team to identify high risk students and initiate connection as well as work as part of emergency mental health response team at Skyline High School, for the period of October 1, 2021, through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $44,560.00.
headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $44,560 for student mental health support at Skyline
summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund will provide one-on-one and group mental health support for students at Skyline High School. It will also work with school teams to identify high-risk students and serve on an emergency mental health response team. The agreement runs from October 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022. The agreement period began before the board vote.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Vincent Yu - Franklin Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement  2021-2022 by and between the District and Vincent Yu, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide additional hours as a community liaison assisting with minor conflict resolution, conducting small group intervention for positive student interactions during the school day, for the period of October 07, 2021 through June 30, 2022, in the additional amount of $5,000.00, increasing the Agreement not to exceed amount from $15,000.00 to $20,000.00.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $5,000 for a community liaison at Franklin Elementary, raising the contract to $20,000
summary: This amendment adds hours for an individual contractor serving as a community liaison at Franklin Elementary School, who helps with minor conflict resolution and leads small-group work on positive student interactions during the school day. It raises the contract limit from $15,000 to $20,000, and all other terms stay the same. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Our Family Coalition - Network 4
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Our Family Coalition, San Francisco, CA, for the latter to provide a professional training series for all Network 4 principals on a weekly basis for 2 hours, covering topics that include inclusive school trainings that will create more welcoming schools and agencies to serve LGBTQ families and their allies. Additionally, principals will implement more equitable practices to serve lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer families and their allies, via Network 4, for the period of April 1, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00.
headline: Pays Our Family Coalition up to $5,000 for LGBTQ-inclusive training for Network 4 principals
summary: Our Family Coalition will lead a weekly two-hour training series for all Network 4 principals on making schools more welcoming and equitable for LGBTQ families and their allies. The agreement runs from April 1 to June 30, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - College Summit dba PeerForward - Fremont High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and College Summit, Inc dba PeerForward, Washington, DC, for the latter to conduct a two (2) hour virtual orientation and Leadership Development session and conduct a Training Workshop that focuses on the ins and outs of the college admissions process, master leadership skills, and community organizing techniques; and post-training, assist participants to execute three powerful campaigns to get their peers to college, as stated in Exhibit A of the Agreement, at Fremont High School, for the period of March 1, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $12,000.00.
headline: Pays PeerForward up to $12,000 for a college-going leadership workshop at Fremont High
summary: College Summit, Inc., doing business as PeerForward, will run a virtual leadership orientation and a training workshop on college admissions, leadership and community organizing at Fremont High School. It will then help participants carry out three campaigns to get their peers to college. The agreement runs from March 1 to June 30, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Community Development Finance - Linked Learning Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Community Development Finance, Oakland, CA, for the latter, as directed by District’s Central Academic Recovery lead, to distribute stipends to students participating in select credit recovery programs as part of District’s set of strategies to address COVID learning loss, via Linked Learning Department, for the period of May 16, 2022, through August 8, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $18,000.00.
headline: Pays Community Development Finance up to $18,000 to distribute credit recovery stipends
summary: Community Development Finance will distribute stipends to students in selected credit recovery programs, as directed by the district's Central Academic Recovery lead. The stipends are part of the district's strategies to address COVID learning loss, through the Linked Learning Department. The agreement runs from May 16 to August 8, 2022. The board is ratifying this agreement.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Student Travel - Chicago, Illinois - National Restorative Justice Conference - Edna Brewer Middle School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0199 - Authorization for Approval of Student Travel - by school site Edna Brewer Middle School, for 20 students and 6 adults, as specified in Out of State Field Trip/Excursion Request, attached, to attend the National Community Restorative Justice Conference in Chicago, Illinois, as described in the itinerary, for the period of July 6, 2022 through July 9, 2022, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves Edna Brewer Middle School trip to a Chicago restorative justice conference at no cost
summary: The Board is asked to approve an out-of-state trip for 20 students and 6 adults from Edna Brewer Middle School to the National Community Restorative Justice Conference in Chicago. The trip would run from July 6 to July 9, 2022. It would be at no cost to the District.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Student Assignment Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide through Youth Beat at KDOL, a fiscal project of the Fund, the production of 11 videos incorporating school personnel and voices that detail the primary offerings of each site, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via Student Assignment Department, for the period of February 1, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00.
headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $25,000 for 11 videos about what each school offers
summary: The district hires the Oakland Public Education Fund, through its Youth Beat at KDOL project, to produce 11 videos featuring school staff and voices that describe what each school site offers. The Student Assignment Department will use them. The work runs from February 1 to June 30, 2022, for no more than $25,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Oakland School of the Arts - J-13A Waiver - Loss of Attendance and Instructional Time - COVID-19 Pandemic
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0083 - Approval of Oakland School of the Arts (OSA) J-13A Waiver.
headline: Approves Oakland School of the Arts waiver request over COVID-19 lost attendance and instruction time
summary: The Board is asked to adopt a resolution approving a J-13A waiver for Oakland School of the Arts. According to the item title, the waiver relates to attendance and instructional time lost during the COVID-19 pandemic. The text states no dollar amount.
outcome_action: Adopted

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - FM3 Research - Office of General Counsel
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and FM3 Research, Oakland, CA, for the latter to conduct survey research among District voters on issues related to a potential parcel tax measure, as specified in Exhibit A, (FM3 Proposal December 8, 2021), via Office of the General Counsel, for the period of January 1, 2022 through May 31, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $36,500.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $36,500 for FM3 Research to survey voters on a possible parcel tax
summary: The Board is approving, after the service period began, an agreement with FM3 Research to survey District voters about a possible parcel tax measure. The Office of the General Counsel manages the work, which runs from January 1 to May 31, 2022. The cost is capped at $36,500.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – N. V. Heathorn Company – The Center Foster School Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Agreement Between Owner and Contractor of Change Order No. 1 by and between the District and N.V. Heathorn Company, Concord, CA, for the latter to provide additional construction services, which consist of repairing a cart wash duct & ceiling, repairing a leaking steam valve and pipes, replace and remove duroblocks, remove old VFDs from the roof, and fix a broken heat recovery pipe connected to refrigeration equipment, for The Center at Foster Project, in the amount of $16,980.00, increasing the contract price from $16,346.00 to $33,326.00 and extending the term of Agreement from September 23, 2021 through December 31, 2021, by 181 days, to June 30, 2022.
headline: Adds $16,980 and 181 days for N.V. Heathorn's extra repairs at The Center at Foster
summary: This change order adds extra construction work at The Center at Foster project: repairing a cart wash duct and ceiling, a leaking steam valve and pipes, and a broken heat recovery pipe, plus removing old equipment from the roof. It raises the contract price from $16,346 to $33,326 and extends the end date by 181 days, to June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Change Order No. 1 Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Data Services, Inc. – Various Sites Door Entry System Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 1 of Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Data Media Services, Inc., Stockton, CA, granting time extension for completion for the Various Sites Door Entry System Project, from December 11, 2021 through February 14, 2022, by 199 days, to September 1, 2022. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Extends the door entry system project deadline by 199 days for Data Media Services, at no added cost
summary: This change order gives Data Media Services, Inc. more time to finish the Various Sites Door Entry System Project, moving the completion date by 199 days to September 1, 2022. The text states no added money. All other terms of the agreement stay the same.
source_issue: The title names the contractor as Data Services, Inc., but the action text names Data Media Services, Inc.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2021-2022 - KNB Solutions, LLC - Technology Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and KNB Solutions LLC, Long Beach, CA, for the latter to support District strategic technology planning efforts by co-coordinating District working groups and contributing to plan documentation and presentations, in the additional amount of $25,000.00, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Agreement from $130,000.00 to $155,000.00, for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022, via the Technology Services Department. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
headline: Adds $25,000 to the KNB Solutions technology planning contract, raising it to $155,000
summary: KNB Solutions helps the district's technology department plan its long-term technology strategy by coordinating working groups and preparing plan documents and presentations. This amendment adds $25,000, raising the contract limit from $130,000 to $155,000 for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Help a Mother Out - Chief Systems and Services Officer
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Help a Mother Out, Oakland, CA, for the latter to improve baby and family well-being by increasing access to diapers for families in need through a network of social service partners with a supply of clean diapers, a requirement to attend most childcare programs, via the Chief Systems and Services Officer, for the period March 30, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $2,000.00.
headline: Approves up to $2,000 for Help a Mother Out to supply diapers to families in need
summary: Help a Mother Out works with social service partners to give families in need access to clean diapers. The agreement runs March 30 through June 30, 2022, with a limit of $2,000. The board is approving it after the start date, as a ratification.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Bay Area Community Resources - Custodial Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Bay Area Community Resources, San Rafael, CA, for the latter to work with the Custodial and Nutrition Services Sustainability Manager on waste prevention program, involving performing site visits, meeting with school team staff to include custodians, nutrition service staff, principals, teachers, and students, making recommendations on infrastructure support; follow up visits to provide needed bins, signage, and other supporting materials; and assist on current program materials and improve on what is in place as well as develop new initiatives, via Custodial Services Department, for the period of September 7, 2021, through July 31, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $28,000.00.
funding_source: 9161 Altamont Education Advisory and 9235 AC Waste Management Authority
headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $28,000 for a school waste prevention program
summary: Bay Area Community Resources will visit schools, meet with custodians, nutrition staff, principals, teachers and students, and recommend ways to reduce waste. It will also provide bins and signs and help build new waste initiatives. The agreement runs September 7, 2021 through July 31, 2022.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Award of Bid#21-108SWC / Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Blenderbox, Inc. - Student Application System - Technology Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution 2122-0228 - Award of Bid … in Response to RFP#21-108SWC, and Services Agreement 2021-2022 to Blenderbox, Inc., New York, NY, in an amount not to exceed Five Hundred Seventy Thousand Dollars ($570,000.00), as the responsive, responsible bidder, for District’s Student Application System (License), via Technology Services Department, for the period May 26, 2022 through June 30, 2025.
headline: Awards Blenderbox up to $570,000 through 2025 for the district's student application system
summary: After a bid process, the board is awarding Blenderbox a contract to license the district's student application system, the online tool families use to apply to schools. The contract may not exceed $570,000 and runs May 26, 2022 through June 30, 2025.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2021-2022 - Claudine Gossett Photography - Chief Systems and Services Officer
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2021-2022 by and between the District and Claudine Gossett Photography, Berkeley, CA, for the latter, bringing professional equipment needed to each site, and under the guidance of the Nutrition Services Project Manager, take photos at seven schools during breakfast and lunch periods and provide Nutrition Services with digital images from which to select photos for printing, via the Office of the Chief of Systems and Services, for the period of April 11, 2022 through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for a photographer to shoot school breakfast and lunch for Nutrition Services
summary: Claudine Gossett Photography brought professional equipment to seven schools to take photos during breakfast and lunch, then gave Nutrition Services digital images to choose from for printing. The agreement runs April 11 through June 30, 2022, with a limit of $5,000. The board is approving it after the start date.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Piggyback Agreement - Lakeshore Learning - Classroom and Office Furniture - Procurement Department
official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education of Resolution No. 2122-0043- Declaring It Is In The Best Of The District To Piggyback On And Enter Into A Contract With Lakeshore Learning Properly Entered Into By Torrance Unified School District for purchase of Classroom and Office Furniture, and approving Piggyback Agreement By and Between Lakeshore Learning, Carlson, CA, and the District, for up to a fiscal year not-to-exceed amount of $1,300,000.00, for the term May 25, 2022 through May 5, 2023.
headline: Buys classroom and office furniture from Lakeshore Learning, up to $1.3M, off another district's contract
summary: The district will buy classroom and office furniture from Lakeshore Learning under a contract that Torrance Unified School District already signed. The district is buying through another agency's existing contract instead of running its own bid. The limit is $1,300,000 for the fiscal year, for May 25, 2022 through May 5, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

headline: Cancels a $15,000 design coach contract in East Bay Innovation Academy's Measure N plan
summary: The Board is asked to approve a change to East Bay Innovation Academy's 2022-23 Measure N spending plan. A $15,000 consultant contract with a design innovation coach is reduced to $0, and the 2023-24 carryover grows from $69,029 to $84,029. The Measure N Commission recommended the change.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Declaring the Futility of Public Bidding and Awarding Purchase Order Contract – Apple, Inc. – Fremont High School New Construction Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Resolution Number 2223-0159 - Declaring the Futility of Public Bidding for the Purchase of Computer Equipment at The Fremont High School Site, and Approving a Contract for that Purchase [with Apple, Inc., Austin, TX, Purchase Order Contract, in the amount of $492,545.89, Education Price Quote No. 2211355883) to procure the Products, specified in Exhibit “A,” of Contract, for Fremont High School New Construction Project, with work scheduled to commence on January 18, 2023, and scheduled to last until June 30, 2023.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Buys $492,545.89 of Apple computer equipment for the new Fremont High School without public bidding
summary: The Board is asked to declare that public bidding is futile for computer equipment at the Fremont High School site and to approve a $492,545.89 purchase order with Apple, Inc. title: Amendment No. 1, Agreement for Architectural Services – HKIT Architects – Glenview Elementary School New Construction Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Agreement for Architectural Services by and between the District and HKIT Architects, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide additional architectural services, with Scope including the design of additional equipment for the supervising station for the Bosch cellular equipment, preparation of corrective measures related to the exposed soil condition below southern site retaining wall, and design services for the footing and anchorage of the three signs; also includes future work to design and document the acoustic improvements to the Multi-Purpose Room in an effort to meet standard for Collaborative For High Performance School (CHPS) base scope, for the Glenview Elementary School New Construction Project, as described in the Proposal dated November 7, 2022, attached to this Amendment, as part of Exhibit A, in an additional not-to-exceed amount of $49,105.50, increasing the Agreement not-to-exceed amount from $29,973.90 to $83,989.95, and extending the term of Agreement from December 16, 2021 through June 30, 2022 to September 1, 2023 (an additional 428 calendar days). All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $49,105.50 to HKIT Architects' contract for Glenview Elementary's new building, through Sept. 2023
summary: This amendment pays HKIT Architects for extra design work on the new Glenview Elementary School: equipment for a cellular alarm monitoring station, fixes for exposed soil below a retaining wall, footing design for three signs, and future sound-proofing design for the multi-purpose room to meet a green-building standard (Collaborative for High Performance Schools). It raises the contract limit to $83,989.95 and extends it by 428 days to September 1, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Agreement for Architectural Services – LCA Architects – Division of State Architect (DSA) Certification of Legacy Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of an Agreement for Architectural Services by and between the District and LCA Architects, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide Basic Services consisting of design services, including landscaping architectural services and landscape irrigation design, civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical engineering services, normally required to complete the Project, including, but not limited to, … facilitate the closeout of the outstanding DSA legacy projects, as described in Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the DSA Certification for Legacy Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $88,160.00, which includes not-to-exceed amounts of $75,600.00 for Basic Services, $7,560.00 for additional services, and $5,000.00 for reimbursable expenses, with work scheduled to commence on January 12, 2023, and scheduled to last until December 30, 2023.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Hires LCA Architects for up to $88,160 to close out old state-review projects
summary: The district would pay LCA Architects up to $88,160 for design and engineering work needed to finish the paperwork for older construction projects with the Division of the State Architect (DSA), the state office that reviews school building plans. The limit is made up of $75,600 for basic services, $7,560 for additional services and $5,000 for reimbursable expenses. Work runs from January 12, 2023 to December 30, 2023.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Change Order No. 1 Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – G & G Builders, Inc.– The OAK at Howard Elementary School Site Improvements Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and G & G Builders, Inc., Livermore, CA, for latter’ scope reduction, from Agreement, as follows: 1) Delete from contract demo and removal of 74'x42' (multi-sport court area) or 3,100 SF of existing asphalt {after investigation this work was not required); 2) Delete from contract new 74'x42' or 3,100 SF (multi-sport court) of new concrete rat-slab (after Investigation this work was not required); 3) Delete to remove (1) basketball hoop (G&G only removed 3 hoops in lieu of 4, as Kaboom already remove done for them} [After the contractor was on board, and after investigation walk with both the contractor and the multi-sport court manufacturer, it was decided that some additional scope was not required. headline: Cuts $53,566.35 from G & G Builders' contract after court work at Howard Elementary proved unnecessary

title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Deco Tech Systems – Oakland High School Security Improvement Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
